## Known biases

Rain-only maps from a model with the drainage system assumed fully working and catch basins clear; parks of 100,000 sq ft or more, non-residential non-commercial lots of 250,000 sq ft or more and lots with railway were masked out, so flooding there is not shown. Areas under 0.25 acre are dropped (with exceptions), and coastal storm surge is not modelled. The publisher says very little observed data on surface flooding exists to check the maps against.

<pre>This scenario reflects approximately two inches of rain falling in one hour (also referred to as the 10-year storm, with approximately 10 percent chance of occurrence in any given year) combined with 2.5 feet of SLR ... </details>

<details><summary>Passage: model</summary>

<pre>The models were built in Innovyze’s InfoWorks ICM software which facilitates coupling of a 1-dimensionsal (1-D) rainfall-runoff and sewer routing component with a 2-dimensional (2D) overland flow and flood visualization component.
Phase 2 modeling developed an H&amp;H model for each hydraulically independent area of the city, resulting in 13 different models</pre>

</details>
